newsitem.title: ISRAEL: U.S. Mideast envoy comes up empty in peace bid.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Mideast envoy comes up empty in peace bid.

text.p: U.S. Middle East point man Dennis Ross heads for home on Friday after coming up empty in his latest bid to breathe new life into deadlocked Israeli-PLO peace moves.
In Lebanon, the last active Arab-Israeli frontline, Israeli planes rocketed suspected Moslem guerrilla targets on Friday, security sources in Lebanon said.
There was no immediate word on casualties. The attack came after pro-Iranian Hizbollah guerrillas killed three Israeli soldiers and wounded seven in fierce clashes in south Lebanon on Thursday night.
A U.S. official said it was expected Ross would leave Israel later on Friday.

All Ross had to show for his nine-day mission was a meeting last week between Israeli and PLO security chiefs that Israel denounced as insufficient and a second meeting between high-level political officials on Wednesday which Palestinians derided as a failure.
In a parting snub, Palestinian President Yasser Arafat declined to meet Ross on the eve of his return to Washington.

Ross doggedly shuttled between the sides but failed to budge them from positions hardened during a two-month peace freeze sparked by Israel's groundbreaking on a Jewish settlement on a disputed Arab East Jerusalem hilltop.
"Ross's mission has failed completely," Marwan Kanafani, a spokesman for Arafat, told Reuters.

"The Israelis refused to stop building and expanding settlements. The Americans were not serious and did not want to interfere. It's like having a man in the ring supporting one of the fighters," Kanafani said.

The PLO demands Israel order a halt to building Har Homa settlement on the windswept hill known to Palestinians as Jabal Abu Ghneim. It sees the settlement as an attempt to pre-empt final peace talks on the status of Jerusalem.

Israeli leaders have said they will not stop work at the East Jerusalem site, insisting Jews have a right to live in all the biblical Land of Israel -- including East Jerusalem, part of the West Bank captured in 1967.
Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu was cautiously upbeat about the results of Wednesday's meeting attended by high-level negotiators.
"I think yesterday's meeting was a preliminary one which creates the basis for additional rounds of talks," Netanyahu told members of his ruling coalition in Tel Aviv on Thursday.
He said the summer session of parliament, due to start next week, would be held "under the sign of a resumption of talks" broken off over the East Jerusalem settlement.
A U.S. embassy spokesman said Ross felt Wednesday's meeting was a "useful...opportunity to hear each other's concerns."
Israeli Foreign Minister David Levy was due to meet U.S. Secretary of State Madeleine Albright in Washington on Friday on the Middle East peace crisis.

"It won't be solved in one conversation or in a day but it seems to me there is a beginning here, and with patience and by sticking to the positions upon which we must stand firm, we can perhaps achieve progress," Netanyahu said.
Netanyahu conditioned resumption of negotiations on a PLO crackdown on "terror" after a Moslem militant killed himself and three Israelis in a Tel Aviv cafe bombing in March.
Netanyahu held talks with Ross on Thursday but a U.S. official said a planned meeting with Arafat was cancelled.

"Arafat has been so disillusioned with the American lack of intervention and lack of seriousness at resolving the crisis that he did not wish to see Ross before he leaves for Washington," said a PLO official who declined to be identified.
